The instrument may not be made available via the open web, nor sent in the message body or as an attachment to survey participants.' and 'Distributing an entire instrument in either the text of an email or as an email attachment is strictly prohibited.' Publishing the six stems in the IRW item-text dataset is exactly making them available via the open web. Per the DSES ruling (2026-09-04) and irw#1955 (2026-09-06) the rights holder's terms override the deposit licence, which here is PLOS CC BY 4.0 and governs the response data only. This is the same shape as the TAS-20 fee block. EXTRACTION WAS OTHERWISE FULLY SOLVED, so a reversal is a transcription, not a restart: the S3 .xlsx's own column headers ARE the item wording ('I feel calm', 'I am tense', 'I feel upset', 'I am relaxed', 'I feel content', 'I am worried') and data/luu_2024_stai6.py melts those six columns by name (var_name='item'), so the live IRW item codes are byte-identical to the source headers -- mapping_basis would have been data_labels with zero inference and Step 5b exempt (code IS the source column name). The option text is equally settled: every cell in all six columns is one of the four literal strings '1. Not at all', '2. Somewhat', '3. Moderately', '4. Very much' and the script extracts the leading integer, so resp 1/2/3/4 map to Not at all / Somewhat / Moderately / Very much, stored RAW (unreversed) -- the paper states 'We reverse scores for three items ("I feel calm", "I am relaxed", and "I feel content"), then sum up the scores of relevant items', a reversal the processing script does not perform. Instructions were not recoverable from the study (the paper prints no participant instructions and the deposit is a data sheet), so instructions would have shipped blank rather than importing Mind Garden's canonical stem.
